newsitem.title: POLAND: Echo plans new ex-rights share issue.
newsitem.headline: Echo plans new ex-rights share issue.

text.p: Polish developer Echo Investment SA said its management would by mid-year ask the general shareholders' meeting to approve a new ex-rights share issue.

It said in a statement that the issue of common shares, with a minimum price of 75 zlotys per share, would amount to about 10 percent of the stock issued so far. The statement said proceeds from the issue would finance Echo's planned investment.
Last year, Echo created a joint-stock company with French and Dutch hotel firms to build 100 budget-class hotels at the cost of some $350 million.

Echo has a 50 percent stake in the new company called Hekon-Hotele Ekonomiczne SA and the remainder is held by French Sphere International SA and Dutch Copron BV. It also said it expected its net profit to soar to 11.2 million zlotys in 1997 from last year's 2.8 million zlotys, the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
Echo said its sales were expected to quadruple to 80 million zlotys in 1997, compared with last year.
